releases.name: NodeSight 3.0.1
releases.body:
## NodeSight 3.0.1

### New

- **Settings for this character only** and **Minimap button** in the sparkle window's **General** tab, at the top right.
- **Hide the minimap button** with Ctrl Shift Left Click on it. **Minimap button** turns it back on.

### Changes

- **Settings for this character only** now offers a reload when you change it, so the switch happens right away.
- **Sparkles page**. Opening it in Options no longer opens the sparkle window; its **Sparkle window** button does.

releases.name: NodeSight 3.0.0
releases.body:
## NodeSight 3.0.0

Blizzard's latest update patched out every way for addons to read the nodes on the minimap, so everything NodeSight did on your minimap no longer works. NodeSight is now the features that still work: sparkles on the things near you, switching between Find Herbs and Find Minerals, and the required skill in a herb's or ore's tooltip.

### New

- **Minimap button** (on by default). Left Click opens the sparkle settings, Shift Left Click NodeSight's settings, Right Click turns all sparkles on or off, and Shift Right Click turns switching on or off. Its tooltip shows the version. Turn it off with **Minimap button** on NodeSight's settings page.
- **Skill on herb and ore items**. Herbs and ore in your bags (and anywhere else you see their tooltip) show the skill they're gathered with, like "Gathered with Mining (65)", in the same colors as the node's tooltip. It goes with **Required skill in tooltips**.
- **NodeSight's logo** in the addon list.

### Changes

- **Minimap features removed**. Scanning, the symbols on the minimap, far sparkles, the arrow, the sounds, the minimap tooltip's skill line, Switch's Pause near a herb or ore, the Advanced page and the bug report are gone.
- **Sparkle settings** are all on the **Sparkles** page and in the sparkle window, like NodeSight Sparkles. **Only for my professions** is on the window's **General** tab.
- **Size of the game's own dots** is removed. If you had changed it, the game's own size comes back.
- **A one-time message** at login explains what changed.

releases.name: NodeSight Sparkles 1.2.3
releases.body:
## NodeSight Sparkles 1.2.3

### New

- **Settings for this character only** (on by default). Untick it to use the same settings on every character. It offers a reload to switch. In the sparkle window's **General** tab.
- **Minimap button** in the sparkle window's **General** tab, and Ctrl Shift Left Click on the button hides it.

### Changes

- **Minimap button tooltip**. It shows the version, and each click in gold and white.
- **Options page**. Opening it no longer opens the sparkle window; its **Sparkle window** button does.

issues.title: Collecting: remember where herbs and ore were gathered
issues.body:
Rewritten for 3.0.0 as one commit on main, without the recorder.

A new Collect.lua remembers the place of each herb or ore you gather (a gathering cast followed by loot from a game object) and marks the places on the world map. Collecting only: nothing is sent or received.

- Saved account-wide in NodeSightDB.nodes, per map and node, one number per place. A place already known adds nothing.
- Settings page Collecting: on/off, world map marks on/off, Forget all.
- The first place remembered says so in chat, and where to turn it off.

Tested in game on build 1.60.1.70938 (deDE), including the Forever herbs Wilted Peacebloom and Stunted Silverleaf.

The old version of this PR learned its spots from the minimap scans, which 3.0.0 removed, so a plain rebase could not work. The old commits are kept in my fork as step4-faint-old.

issues.title: Scan stand-in: zone-dependent tint causes light/dark flicker; Line regions (routes) vanish during scans
issues.body:
**Version:** NodeSight 2.0.6, WoW Forever 1.60.1 (build 70888), "Map while scanning" on (the 2.0.6 default)

While a scan runs, the stand-in that replaces the real minimap has two visible differences from it. We measured both and worked around them in another addon. A fix in NodeSight would be cleaner, so here is the data.

### 1. Stand-in tint: the needed tint depends on the zone

The minimap tiles in the stand-in use one fixed `MINIMAP_TINT = { 0.87, 0.84, 0.80 }` (NodeSight.lua, StandArt/Put). We compared the same scene with and without the stand-in: a screenshot of the real minimap, then burst screenshots during a scan (CTRL-O) with the player standing still, and the mean colour over a 17×17 grid (289 points) of the 218×218 px minimap interior. Stand-in frames are easy to tell apart, because their pins have no white triangle.

| Zone (uiMapID) | Real minimap R/G/B | Stand-in R/G/B | Tint that matches the real map |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Barrens (1413) | ratio stand-in/real: R 0.929, G 1.072, B 1.087 | too dull | ≈ 0.937 / 0.784 / 0.736 |
| Alterac Mountains (1416) | 49 / 50 / 34 | **61 / 58 / 37** (~20 % brighter) | ≈ 0.707 / 0.729 / 0.749 |
| Hillsbrad Foothills, Darrow Hill (1424) | 39 / 44 / 23 | 52 / 47 / 22 | ≈ 0.657 / 0.779 / 0.808 (player may have moved slightly) |

So in some zones the stand-in is too dull and in others too red or bright. No single constant fits.

**What the user sees:** timer scans run about every 2.8 s with ~35 ms gaps in which the real map is back (frame sampler on `Minimap:IsMouseClickEnabled()` and the stand-in's visibility). With the brightness difference, each swap shows as a light/dark flicker of the whole minimap. With a matching tint per zone, the swap is barely visible.

**Possible fix:** a tint per zone (uiMapID) or per continent instead of one constant, perhaps with a user setting. Alternatively, if the engine's minimap lighting can be read from an API, use that.

### 2. Line regions (e.g. Polestar routes) vanish during a scan

The stand-in copies `Texture` regions of the minimap's children, but not `Line` regions. Route lines drawn as Lines on minimap children, such as Polestar's navigation route (18 lines in our test), disappear for the length of every scan and come back afterwards. That is another visible jump.

**Workaround we used:** outside scans, store each Line of the minimap's direct children (start/end points, texture/atlas, colour, thickness, draw layer, alpha). During a scan, draw copies on our own frame at the minimap's home rect, and keep it up for 0.3 s after a scan ends so the 35 ms gaps between timer scans don't blink. It works, but copying Lines into the stand-in itself would be cleaner.

### 3. Smaller observations

- On the first frame(s) of a scan, the tiles briefly show `MINIMAP_TINT` before any later recolour (only relevant for addons adjusting the tint).
- Pins in the stand-in also get `MINIMAP_TINT`. Your red "too hard" tint on pins is separate and should stay, which is why we only recolour pins that carry `MINIMAP_TINT`.

The numbers come from screenshots at 2560×1440 (UI scale unchanged), measured with a frame sampler and burst shots. Not measured: other zones, night/day, indoor maps. Happy to measure more zones if that helps.

issues.title: [Bug] Minimap markers ignore settings, incorrect node positions and direction arrow
issues.body: ## Summary I'm experiencing several issues with NodeSight's minimap markers and node positioning in WoW Forever. Some markers appear despite being disabled, some do not follow the selected visual style, and detected node positions seem inaccurate. The direction arrow also appears to use these incorrect positions. I'm using EllesmereUI with a square minimap and GatherMate. ## Issues observed ### 1. Minimap symbols are displayed even when disabled The **"Herb and ore symbols"** option is unchecked in NodeSight's settings, but additional node symbols still appear on the minimap. **Expected:** NodeSight's herb and ore symbols should be hidden when this option is disabled. **Screenshots:** - `Node1.jpeg`: Minimap showing the unwanted symbols. --------------- - `Node3.jpeg`: NodeSight settings with "Herb and ore symbols" unchecked. ### 2. Solid red markers instead of thin rings Some node markers appear as large, solid red circles. However, my minimap appearance settings are configured as follows: - Symbol shape: **Round, slim gold ring** - Skill colors: **Colored ring** - Symbol size: **11** - Size of the game's own dots: **100** I would expect the relevant NodeSight markers to use thin outlined rings rather than solid red circles. I'm not entirely sure whether these red circles originate from NodeSight itself or from an interaction with another addon. **Screenshots:** - `Node2.jpeg`: Red markers visible on the minimap. --------------- - `Node4.jpeg`: Selected minimap appearance settings. ### 3. Detected node positions appear incorrect When NodeSight is active and scanning, additional node markers appear on the minimap. Comparing the minimap before and after these markers appear, some locations seem inaccurate or shifted relative to the actual tracking dots and the GatherMate markers. I understand that NodeSight scans the game's native tracking dots rather than reading GatherMate's database directly. My concern is therefore not the data source itself, but the apparent mismatch between the detected and displayed positions. **Expected:** NodeSight's detected node positions should align with the corresponding in-game minimap tracking dots. **Screenshots:** - `Node6.jpeg`: Minimap showing the existing markers. --------------- - `Node7.jpeg`: Additional markers visible with NodeSight, including apparent positional discrepancies. ### 4. Direction arrow points toward incorrect node positions The direction arrow for the nearest herb or ore also seems to be affected by the positioning issue. It appears to use the same inaccurate node coordinates, resulting in directions that do not match the actual gathering locations. **Expected:** The arrow should point toward the actual detected node position, not toward an incorrectly offset minimap marker. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Enable herb or ore tracking in WoW Forever. 2. Use NodeSight with a square minimap (EllesmereUI in my case). 3. Disable **"Herb and ore symbols"** in NodeSight. 4. Check whether additional node symbols remain visible. 5. Set the symbol appearance to **"Round, slim gold ring"** and **"Colored ring"**, then compare the displayed markers. 6. I noticed that issue #15 reported a change to the minimap scanning behavior after a recent WoW Forever client update. I'm mentioning it in case there is a connection, although I cannot confirm that the problems share the same cause. issues.title: Add a recorder for what the scans did each session
issues.body:
Keeps numbers on every scan of a session in NodeSightDB.sessions (the last 12 sessions, 400 scans each): spots, seconds, frames, the slowest frame, finds, why it stopped, how far the mouse moved, whether a mouse button was held, and whether a tooltip or a mob was under the mouse as it started. issues.title: Add a setup window on first launch
issues.body:
Hi Krelock, here's the setup menu we talked about. It's a first draft, happy to change anything.

## What it does
A short two-step window that helps players dial in the scans instead of one default for everyone.

**1. How much may scans interrupt you?**
- **Quiet (recommended):** scan by distance every 40 yards, only while the mouse is still, stop as soon as the mouse moves, wait 5 s after fights to loot. This is the setup that made the scans almost unnoticeable for me.
- **Balanced:** NodeSight's current defaults, unchanged.
- **Most finds:** your existing *Most scans* preset (every 5 s, also standing still and in combat).

**2. What should NodeSight show?** Minimap symbols, arrow, sparkles on herbs and ore, sound for new finds. The boxes start from the current settings.

## When it shows
- Once after the first loading screen of a **fresh install**, in place of the scan notice (waits for combat to end, respects the *Popups* setting).
- Any time from a new **Setup** button next to *Bug report*.
- Existing users keep their settings and see nothing new unless they click Setup.
- **Skip** applies Quiet and leaves everything else alone.

## Changes
- New `Setup.lua` (in the look of your other popups), added to the .toc before `Settings.lua`
- `NodeSight.lua`: remembers a first install and opens the setup instead of the scan notice (+7 lines)
- `Settings.lua`: the Setup button (+15 lines)
- No version bump or What's New entry, I left that to you.

## Tested
In game on Forever (German client): both pages, all choices, Back / Next / Done, the Setup button. No Lua errors.

## Open questions
- Should Quiet also become a preset in the Scanning page's dropdown? Right now picking it there shows *Custom*.
- Would you like existing users to see it once too (e.g. after the next update)?

issues.title: Scan as you move breaks the minimap's drawing while walking (minimap alpha 0)
issues.body:
With "Scan as you move" on, the minimap terrain draws wrong while walking: dark streaks and patches that flicker. It goes back to normal when I stand still. Turning "Scan as you move" off fixes it.

Seen in Silverpine Forest around 47.7, 40.9 (near The Sepulcher). Same on D3D12 and D3D11. NodeSight 1.8.1, client 1.60.1.70862.

Likely cause: during a scan, `Disguise()` sets `Minimap:SetAlpha(0)` (NodeSight.lua:1174) and `KeyPlace()` moves the minimap with `AdjustPointsOffset`. The client has a bug where the minimap redraws wrong if it redraws while its alpha is below 1: ClassicWoWCommunity/forever-bugs#155. Walking makes it redraw, so a scan at the wrong moment leaves it broken until the next redraw.

Maybe hiding it another way during the scan would avoid it (for example covering it, or clipping it with an empty mask), so its alpha stays at 1.

issues.title: [Bug] URGENT: no minimap symbols since client 1.60.1.70862 — UpdateMouseoverAtPoint no longer moves the probe
issues.body:
**Urgent:** since today's Forever client patch, NodeSight draws no symbols at all. Every tracked herb stays a plain yellow dot.

## Cause (tested)
`Minimap:UpdateMouseoverAtPoint` no longer moves the mouseover. After it, `C_TooltipInfo.GetMinimapMouseover()` always returns whatever the **real** cursor is over, whatever point is passed. So the scan sees one name at every grid point and can't place anything.

I ran a test addon that does the same probe as `Probe()` in NodeSight.lua, with Find Herbs on (2383), herbs on the minimap, and the real cursor resting on one dot:

| Test (9×9 grid over the minimap) | Result |
|---|---|
| `(left+x)*effectiveScale`, `SetUsingSoftCursor(true)` (NodeSight's way) | 81/81 points: `Briarthorn\nGrave Moss` (the dot under the real cursor) |
| Same, without `SetUsingSoftCursor` | 81/81 same name |
| UI units (no scale) | 81/81 same name |
| Physical pixels | 81/81 same name |
| One point per frame, read on the next frame | 81/81 same name |

A full NodeSight-style grid (1369 points, step 8) earlier returned `Kingsblood` at all 1369 points. No Lua errors were raised: `scriptErrors` was on, and an error handler was hooked.

- Methods exist: `Minimap.UpdateMouseoverAtPoint` and `Minimap.SetUsingSoftCursor` are both present.
- Not a scale problem: minimap effective scale 0.64, UI 2866×1200, physical 3440×1440.
- Lueur and RareScanner use the same probe and show nothing either.

## Environment
- Client build **1.60.1.70862**. It was installed today, 2026-11-07, at about 09:05 UTC; the previous build was 70840 or earlier.
- NodeSight 1.7.0. I diffed it against 1.6.2: the scan code is unchanged, so this isn't from your update.
- enUS client, EllesmereUI minimap, no rotation. Runs on Linux through Proton (UMU + GE-Proton).
- Settings are defaults: `scan`, `mapIcons` on.

## Not established
- Whether Blizzard turned the soft-cursor probe off on purpose or by accident.
- Whether it also fails on Windows. I can only test on Linux/Proton, though the probe gives the same result in every mode above.

issues.title: Switch: by the way walked, with pauses, areas and a check of each switch (#12)
issues.body:
This is the switch rework from #12. Thanks for the quick answer there! It follows your notes: the settings get their own Switch page, and battlegrounds are off by default.

Every switch costs a global cooldown. Until now it came every 15 yards and didn't look at what you're doing, so on a mount it came very often, and it could take the global cooldown away right before a spell, a gather or an attack. Now the switch comes after a way you choose, pauses when you're about to do something, and checks that it worked.

The five commits build on each other and can be read one by one:

1. **Move the switch's mute into Switch.lua:** NodeSight.lua is close to Lua's limit of 200 local variables, so the switch lives in a new file. This commit only moves the mute there, nothing changes in the game.
2. **By the way walked:** A new Switch page with "Measure distance in": percent of the minimap (40 % of the view radius by default), yards (60 by default) or seconds on the move (8 by default). Only the chosen measure's slider shows. The way is time moved times speed, so it needs no map position. No switch in combat, while standing still, on a flight path, while dead or during the global cooldown. The old "Yards between switches" setting goes.
3. **Pauses:** Switching pauses while you cast, gather or loot, while a spell waits for a target or something is on the cursor, while stealthed, near a herb or ore with a symbol, after your own spells and after dismounting, and while a living enemy within about 40 yards is your target. Each pause can be set on the Switch page, and each tooltip says why switching waits.
4. **Areas and "Only while mounted":** A checkbox each for the open world, dungeons, raids and battlegrounds. Battlegrounds are off by default. "Only while mounted" is off by default.
5. **Check of each switch:** A second after a switch, NodeSight checks that the other finder is on. After two failed switches in a row it stops switching for a minute. A loading screen, mounting or dismounting, a switch by hand or turning the switch off and on ends the stop early.

The commit messages have the details.

Some notes on the behaviour:

- **After the one-minute stop:** The way keeps growing during the stop, so the next switch comes right after it ends.
- **Range to an enemy:** The game doesn't always give an addon an exact distance to an enemy. Then NodeSight asks the game's range checks: the interact ranges, items from LibRangeCheck-3.0's list (5 to 45 yards) and your own spells up to 60 yards. One yes in a range is enough, and a spell's no never counts. That's why the setting says "about".
- **GatherLite:** With GatherLite 8.2.3 and its option to turn gathering tracking on automatically, GatherLite turns its preferred finder back on after every change and every 5 seconds, so it fights the switch. With that option off, the switch works as intended.

Tested in game: the distance measures, the Switch page with only the chosen slider showing, and that a finder switch doesn't stop sitting or eating. Not yet tested in game: the range checks against enemies (which checks answer for enemies and in which order they turn as you walk away) and which spellbook ranges the client reports, for example for hunter shots with Hawk Eye.

issues.title: Settings: Automatic names the minimap shape it found
issues.body:
A small follow-up to #11. On Automatic, NodeSight decides itself whether it scans the minimap as round or square, but the "Minimap shape" setting didn't show what it decided. Now the Automatic choice names it in brackets: "Automatic (Round)", "Automatic (Square)" or "Automatic (Mixed)" for a minimap with both round and square corners. So players can see whether Automatic got their minimap right, or whether to choose Square by hand.

The shape is asked for each time the choices are built. Round and Square stay as they are, and the saved value doesn't change. The Dropdown helper in Settings.lua now also takes a function for its choices.

It's one commit on main and independent of #13. Both PRs touch Settings.lua, but they merge without a conflict in either order.

issues.title: Proposal: smarter timing for the herb/ore switch
issues.body:
The switch between herbs and ore is a real help while farming, because it shows both kinds of nodes on the minimap. There is one limit in the game itself that I keep running into: a tracking switch is a spell cast, and the client gives no way to switch without one, so every switch triggers the global cooldown. With the current 15 yards the switch fires every few seconds on foot, and more often once we have mounts (or tauren). In practice the GCD is running most of the time, and when you target an enemy an ability like Charge is sometimes not available in that moment. I hit the same thing in the beta, on foot, with another addon that switches the same way, so this is not specific to NodeSight. Today combat is the only situation in which the switch pauses, and I think a few more pauses would make it feel smoother.

I would like to rework this part, and before I write any code I'd like to ask whether and how you'd want it. This is what I have in mind:

- **Distance:** a percentage of the minimap's view radius instead of fixed yards, adjustable from 20 to 100 %, default 60 %. A herb or ore of the other kind that appears at the edge right after a switch is then still 40 % of the radius ahead at the next switch. The distance counts the path travelled (time moving × speed), so farming in a small loop still switches.
- **Pauses while busy:** no switch while casting, gathering, looting or holding a spell or item on the cursor (one on/off setting for all four); with a living enemy targeted within about 40 yards (adjustable up to 60, or off); near a herb or ore (default 10 yards, adjustable up to 40, or off); while stealthed (on by default); and for a few seconds after your own cast (default 3, adjustable up to 10, or off).
- **Always paused:** standing still, combat, GCD, flight paths, dead or ghost. These have no setting, because a switch never helps there. Standing still is on the list because nothing new shows up on the minimap while you stand, and a cast in place might interrupt eating, drinking or Feign Death.
- **Where:** one on/off setting per zone type (open world, dungeons, raids, battlegrounds), all on by default, since some dungeons (Maraudon, Uldaman, Blackrock Spire) and even battlegrounds like Alterac Valley have herbs and ore. Plus an option to switch only while mounted (off by default).
- **Failures:** if a switch has no effect twice in a row, it stops until a loading screen, mounting or a manual tracking change (or after 60 seconds).
- **Settings:** a separate page "Switch" (the checkbox stays on the main page too, like the arrow's), 11 new keys. `switchYards` would go away.
- **Code:** a new file `Switch.lua`; `NodeSight.lua` loses the old `Switch()` and gets no new locals. The switch itself still happens only between two scans, so a scan is never cut in half.

A few parts need a check in the live client after launch (whether `UnitDistanceSquared` returns a distance for enemies, and whether the finder spells work in druid forms and Ghost Wolf). Until then those parts would fall back to simpler checks.

Questions:

1. Is that number of settings fine with you, or would you prefer fewer (for example one "pause when busy" checkbox for all pauses)?
2. A separate settings page, or keep everything on the main page?
3. I'd send it as one PR with five commits, each with its own settings: (1) move the mute code to `Switch.lua` unchanged, (2) the distance and the always-on pauses, which on their own already make switches much rarer, (3) the pauses you can set, (4) zones and "only while mounted", (5) the stop after failures. Would that work for you, or would you rather have separate PRs?
4. Are you working on this part yourself, or is there anything you would rather keep for yourself?

issues.title: Scan the corners of a square minimap
issues.body:
NodeSight scans only the circle of the minimap, so on a square minimap the herbs and ore in the corners never get a symbol. This PR lets the scan follow the minimap's shape. Three commits, each works on its own:

1. **Scan the corners of a square minimap.** UI addons that make the minimap square say so through `GetMinimapShape()`, the convention LibDBIcon and HereBeDragons use. NodeSight reads it with LibDBIcon-1.0's table of round and square quarters, so mixed shapes (`CORNER-*`, `SIDE-*`, `TRICORNER-*`) work too. The coarse and fine grids, the edge search and the "still on the minimap" check follow that shape.
2. **Minimap shape setting.** A dropdown on the Symbols page (Automatic, Round, Square) for UI addons that make the minimap square without saying so.
3. **EllesmereUI.** Its minimap is widely used and doesn't set `GetMinimapShape`. On Automatic, NodeSight asks EllesmereUIMinimap for the shape it draws. A cut at the top and bottom (its 4:3 map, and its Forever Square with the zone title bar) is read from `Minimap:GetHitRectInsets()`, which EllesmereUI sets for every cut. This goes through `EllesmereUI._ModuleNS`, which is EllesmereUI's own registry, not an API, so I see it as a stopgap until EllesmereUI sets `GetMinimapShape` itself. If it changes, NodeSight falls back to `GetMinimapShape` and then to round, and the dropdown still works. If you'd rather not depend on another addon's internals, commit 3 can be dropped without touching the others.

Notes:

- As you asked in #3, the new code and tables are in a new file, `MinimapShape.lua`, and `NodeSight.lua` gets no new locals. The load check also needs `ns.MinimapQuarters` now.
- A round minimap, a missing `GetMinimapShape` or a shape it doesn't know behave exactly as in 1.5.1: same grid points, same probes, same symbols. I checked this against 1.5.1 with busted specs (not part of this PR).
- On a square minimap a scan probes about a third to a half more points, depending on Scan detail. Reading the shape costs a few table lookups per frame.
- Not tested in the live client yet.

issues.title: Stop errors in the per-frame work from repeating every frame
issues.body:
Nothing guarded the per-frame work in `OnUpdate`. An error there came again every frame until a reload, and a failed minimap probe also left the pretend mouse on (`Minimap:SetUsingSoftCursor(true)`). Four commits, one per place:

1. **Minimap scan:** `OnUpdate` runs `ScanSome` through `xpcall` with the game's error handler, so the error is still reported, but once per try. Then it lets go of the pretend mouse, drops the scan and waits a long pause (`WAIT * SLEEP`, with `rested` back to 0 so standing still stretches it at most 4 times). Moving, loot or a fight's end try again sooner, as after any scan.
2. **Level of a far node:** `world.Level` probes the minimap too. The probe and the tooltip call now run in a `pcall`, the pretend mouse is let go either way, and then the error goes on, so it is still reported and not swallowed.
3. **Far marker:** `world.Update` runs through `xpcall` as well. After an error, `world.stopped` keeps the far sparkles off until the next reload: Blizzard's marker shows again and the sparkles go out with their animations stopped (`world.Out`, your existing hiding code, now a function of its own). The stop is checked at the top of `world.Update`, so the direct call from `UpdateScanner` on a settings change can't bring them back either. If they had marked a node, your own map pin and tracked quest come back (`world.Back`) once it's safe to touch the pin, with the same `busy` check as the rest of `world.Update` (not in a fight, not with the world map open). The `busy` line moves up so it is computed once for both. A pin they never touched is left alone, and putting yours back is tried only once.
4. **Symbols and arrow:** `Follow` and `UpdateArrow` run through `xpcall` too. After an error the symbols are cleared (`markers = {}`, as elsewhere), the arrow hides with no target left, and the scan waits the same long pause. With no symbols both have nothing to do, so a lasting error comes back once per pause.

When nothing fails, everything runs as before. No new file-level locals.

issues.title: Recognize Nightmare Moss, Dreamroot and Star Lotus as herbs
issues.body:
Nightmare Moss, Dreamroot and Star Lotus are Forever herb nodes ([439557](https://www.wowhead.com/forever/object=439557), [439627](https://www.wowhead.com/forever/object=439627) and [439762](https://www.wowhead.com/forever/object=439762) on Wowhead, Herbalism 125, 205 and 250). `NEEDED` already lists their skill, but `NodeKind` only knows herbs whose name ends in an entry of `HERB_ICONS` or `HERB_OTHER`. So in every language they showed up only after the first gather taught the addon their name.

They have no item icon of their own, so they join Moonroot in `HERB_OTHER` and get the plain herb symbol.

**Not covered:** esMX and zhCN have no translation yet for Nightmare Moss and Star Lotus, ptBR for Star Lotus and zhTW for Dreamroot. On those clients the addon still learns these herbs on the first gather, as before.
